items.title: Protect interests of students: Supreme Court asks CBSE to address OSM evaluation issues
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to explore ways to protect the interests of students facing difficulties in entrance-based admissions due to their scores under the Board’s new On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluating answer sheets. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told that some students had cleared their CBSE examinations and had subsequently appeared for entrance examinations for other courses. However, they had not secured the minimum marks required for admission because of their CBSE scores, and some of the courses had already commenced. The plea linked the lesser marks/ scores to the irregularities in OSM evaluation system. The Bench then asked CBSE to examine the issue and find out how the interests of such students could be protected. "Please find out how can you protect their interest," the Court said before adjourning the matter. items.title: Sumit Sarkar’s unfinished argument with history
items.summary: Sometime in 2000, I lost my copy of Sumit Sarkar’s Modern India in the Hindu College hostel at Delhi University. It was unfortunate. I remember looking for another copy in the library but without any success. I was somehow in a hurry to finish reading it, so I bought a new copy. It was a brown-covered Macmillan copy of the classic. I wasn’t a student of history at the university; his work was there in the interdisciplinary readings. I finished reading the book soon. It has been a matter of wonder for me that Sarkar’s book, which otherwise was a dense and academic study, had engrossed me. The reason wasn’t far to seek. You had to just look at the rest of the bookshelf of readings for the same course. Even if some place the book within a broad Marxist corpus on modern Indian history, Sarkar’s work was remarkable in finding its way out of that dogmatic frame. In doing so, he found a subaltern footing in retelling “history from below”, opening up the narrow economistic gaze of Marxism to social and cultural registers, and noting even the ordinariness of agents shaping modern Indian history. items.title: Husband called wife barren, wife called husband impotent: What Allahabad HC held
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently observed that addressing a wife as “barren woman” may not constitute cruelty under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) when there is exchange of “filthy verbal blows” from both sides. items.title: Karnataka High Court permits Hindu Jagarana Vedike’s Mysuru torchlight procession on Independence Day eve
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday permitted the Hindu Jagarana Vedike to conduct its ‘Akhanda Bharata Sankalpa Dina’ torchlight procession in Mysuru on the eve of Independence Day [ Hindu Jagrana Vedike & another vs The Commissioner of Police & another ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj , however, made it clear that the procession's organisers would be held responsible if any untoward incident takes place during the march. The Court has directed the police to provide necessary security for the procession from RMC Ganesha Temple to Dodda Gadiyara Circle, which will commence at 5:30 PM and conclude at 7:30 PM on August 14. The Court passed the order after rejecting the State's argument that there is possibility of unlawful incidents arising during the march since some of the programme's organisers had a history of anti-social activities and have criminal cases pending against them. The Court opined that this cannot be a ground to prevent them from participating in Independence Day celebrations. items.title: Supreme Court quashes FIRs against Samay Raina, 4 other comedians over remarks about disabled persons
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashed criminal cases filed against YouTuber-comedian Samay Raina and four other comedians over insensitive remarks made on the show India's Got Latent about persons with disabilities. A Bench Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order. Apart from Raina, the others who have been given relief in connection with this case are Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar alias Sonali Aditya Desai, and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The Court today appreciated the efforts made by Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar to organise shows for the benefit of persons with disabilities. " Once there are genuine efforts positive results are bound to be there. They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in positive direction, there will be positive output," the Bench said. The Court proceeded to quash criminal cases filed against them over insensitve remarks against disabled persons.
